reviewNote: Drafted by Claude for faculty review from the Carson-Newman scenario. Not validated teaching content.
summary: Healthy adult for a lap umbilical hernia. The CN Standard IV induction rubric case: prove mask ventilation before neuromuscular blockade and keep ventilating through onset. The full beard is the one airway wrinkle.

decision.rationale: Elective case, appropriately fasted, no optimization needed.

redFlags.finding: Full beard: mask seal may be hard
redFlags.evidence: Nursing and PAT notes document a full beard; he will not shave.
redFlags.implication: Bag mask ventilation can leak, and this rubric requires proving mask ventilation before the blocker.
redFlags.action: Two hand mask hold, oral airway, petroleum gel or a clear dressing over the beard, confirm ventilation on capnography before the blocker.

redFlags.evidence: Wife reports snoring, no witnessed apneas.
redFlags.implication: Possible undiagnosed OSA; mask ventilation and opioid sensitivity.
redFlags.action: STOP-BANG, oral airway ready, opioid sparing analgesia.

planItems.item: Standard IV induction: preoxygenate, induce, confirm mask ventilation, then the neuromuscular blocker
Direct or video laryngoscopy with ETT, confirm with EtCO2
Cefazolin 2 g within 60 min of incision

boothComplications.why: Airway instrumentation at a light plane
